data.note:
Reflection: specimen is mitomycin C — PubChem CID 5746, ChEMBL CHEMBL105 DNA inhibitor, agreeing with BBBC021 DNA damage.

I was wrong. Mid-dose wells consistently showed the true biology: nuc_area z 23-26, nuc_dna_integrated z up to 13.96, frac_large_nucleus z 8-9, and atlas 9/10 DNA damage/replication neighbors at sims 0.87-0.967 (e9,e15). I overweighted one sparse high-dose well (155 cells, cell_count z -6.74) with tub_glcm_contrast z 25.1 and 8/10 stabilizer neighbors (e8).

In retrospect the tubulin brightening was secondary to extreme spreading/enlargement (cell_area z 10.25) and low density, not bundles. Literature confirms DNA crosslink mechanism: mitomycin C-DNA interstrand crosslinks and XPA recognition (PMID 17512921), differential toxicity of adducts (PMID 20798760), DSBs enhanced by pol-kappa loss (PMID 41199376), reductive activation (PMID 19791750, PMID 9369485) and crosslink replication bypass (PMID 34262911).

Lesson: require replicate high-dose wells and normalize tubulin intensity for cell spreading before calling stabilizer when DNA features dominate lower doses.

reflection.text:
I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at 0.78 based on the 10 uM well w_b962c28c9c with tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1 in only 155 cells, the high-dose atlas match of 8/10 stabilizers, and monotonic tub_glcm_contrast/tub_mean rise with rho=+1.00. The unblinded truth is mitomycin C, a DNA inhibitor that forms interstrand crosslinks (PMID 17512921) and induces double-strand breaks (PMID 41199376) that block replication (PMID 34262911).

What I got right but discounted was the mid-dose nuclear signal: nuc_area z=+23.6 to +26.7 with increased nuc_dna_integrated and frac_large_nucleus at 0.3-3 uM, plus atlas isolations pointing to DNA damage and DNA replication and repeated microscopist calls of Aurora kinase inhibitors/DNA damage with falling cell count. I acquired the high dose first and anchored on the early stabilizer visual call, then treated the mid-dose enlargement as secondary polyploid slippage without ever testing a DNA-damage readout.

The error was overweighting a sparse, cytotoxic high-dose texture measurement over a multi-well consensus: 155 cells at 10 uM versus 635-637 cells at mid doses with rho=-1.00 for cell count makes texture contrast unreliable as a primary-MoA marker. Future runs should require DNA-content distributions and replicated mid-dose atlas agreement before accepting a single high-dose cytoskeletal match.
what_was_right: Mid-dose wells showed extreme nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z +23.6 to +26.7, nuc_major_axis z +12-15, frac_large_nucleus z +9.5) with high nuc_dna_integrated, consistent with genotoxic polyploidy.
Atlas comparisons isolated to mid doses pointed away from stabilizers to DNA damage / DNA replication (e9: 5/10 damage, e15: 5/10 replication, e6 mixed damage/replication).
Microscopist repeatedly raised Aurora kinase inhibitors and DNA damage and cell count fell monotonically (rho -1.00), signaling arrest/slippage rather than primary tubulin stabilization.
what_was_wrong: Overweighted single high-dose well w_b962c28c9c (10 uM, 155 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z +25.1, tub_std z +14.2) and its 8/10 stabilizer atlas match despite sparsity and toxicity.

Interpreted monotonic tub_glcm_contrast/tub_mean rise (rho +1.00) as stabilizer-specific without measuring gamma-H2AX, DNA-content, or mitotic markers to exclude DNA crosslinker-induced reorganization.

Locked hypothesis at 0.78 for Microtubule stabilizers by framing large nuclei as secondary slippage, ignoring that non-monotonic nuc_area and flat nuc_dna_integrated dose-responses fit DNA-damage arrest.

citations.claim: Mitomycin C forms DNA interstrand crosslinks preferentially bound by repair factor XPA.
Mitomycin C induces DNA double-strand breaks in vivo.
Interstrand crosslink-containing DNA blocks replication and requires coordinated cut-and-bypass repair.

reflection.next_experiment: Low-dose titration (0.03-1 uM) with gamma-H2AX/53BP1 foci counts plus DNA-content flow cytometry and SiR-tubulin washout imaging to test for primary DNA crosslink damage with secondary mitotic slippage versus direct microtubule stabilization.

## Reflection

I concluded Microtubule stabilizers at 0.78 based on the 10 uM well w_b962c28c9c with tub_glcm_contrast z=+25.1 in only 155 cells, the high-dose atlas match of 8/10 stabilizers, and monotonic tub_glcm_contrast/tub_mean rise with rho=+1.00. The unblinded truth is mitomycin C, a DNA inhibitor that forms interstrand crosslinks (PMID 17512921) and induces double-strand breaks (PMID 41199376) that block replication (PMID 34262911).

What I got right but discounted was the mid-dose nuclear signal: nuc_area z=+23.6 to +26.7 with increased nuc_dna_integrated and frac_large_nucleus at 0.3-3 uM, plus atlas isolations pointing to DNA damage and DNA replication and repeated microscopist calls of Aurora kinase inhibitors/DNA damage with falling cell count. I acquired the high dose first and anchored on the early stabilizer visual call, then treated the mid-dose enlargement as secondary polyploid slippage without ever testing a DNA-damage readout.

The error was overweighting a sparse, cytotoxic high-dose texture measurement over a multi-well consensus: 155 cells at 10 uM versus 635-637 cells at mid doses with rho=-1.00 for cell count makes texture contrast unreliable as a primary-MoA marker. Future runs should require DNA-content distributions and replicated mid-dose atlas agreement before accepting a single high-dose cytoskeletal match.

What was right:
- Mid-dose wells showed extreme nuclear enlargement (nuc_area z +23.6 to +26.7, nuc_major_axis z +12-15, frac_large_nucleus z +9.5) with high nuc_dna_integrated, consistent with genotoxic polyploidy.
- Atlas comparisons isolated to mid doses pointed away from stabilizers to DNA damage / DNA replication (e9: 5/10 damage, e15: 5/10 replication, e6 mixed damage/replication).
- Microscopist repeatedly raised Aurora kinase inhibitors and DNA damage and cell count fell monotonically (rho -1.00), signaling arrest/slippage rather than primary tubulin stabilization.

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted single high-dose well w_b962c28c9c (10 uM, 155 cells, tub_glcm_contrast z +25.1, tub_std z +14.2) and its 8/10 stabilizer atlas match despite sparsity and toxicity.
- Interpreted monotonic tub_glcm_contrast/tub_mean rise (rho +1.00) as stabilizer-specific without measuring gamma-H2AX, DNA-content, or mitotic markers to exclude DNA crosslinker-induced reorganization.
- Locked hypothesis at 0.78 for Microtubule stabilizers by framing large nuclei as secondary slippage, ignoring that non-monotonic nuc_area and flat nuc_dna_integrated dose-responses fit DNA-damage arrest.

Proposed next experiment: Low-dose titration (0.03-1 uM) with gamma-H2AX/53BP1 foci counts plus DNA-content flow cytometry and SiR-tubulin washout imaging to test for primary DNA crosslink damage with secondary mitotic slippage versus direct microtubule stabilization.
